title: Horizon Medical Research - QBR talking points & renewal playbook
content:
Purpose: Draft narrative + slide/script for upcoming QBR with Horizon Medical Research (HMR). This is a working doc — contains proposed slide-by-slide speaker notes, renewal health assessment, and a simple renewal tracker. Primary goals: reinforce value, address operational friction points, and map to an upsell path for advanced observability and Dedicated capacity.

Meeting context
- Customer: Horizon Medical Research (clinical research org, heavy inference workloads for de-identified clinical summarization and cohort search).
- Renewal window: 2025-02-14 (enterprise contract annual renewal).
- Primary contacts: Dr. Lena Kaur (CTO), Mateo Ruiz (Head of Data Platform), Olivia Park (Procurement).
- Current tier: Hosted API with moderate concurrency, 600M tokens/month; trialing a 1-node Dedicated pool for peak hours.

QBR Objectives (what we want from this meeting)
1) Validate ROI: show token-cost trends, response latency improvements from prefix caching experiments.
2) Surface operational wins and pain points: address reported KV cache evictions and rate limited training jobs.
3) Secure renewal + propose pilot for Dedicated committed capacity (6-month pilot; measured SLO uplift).
4) Surface roadmap alignment: privacy features (HSM/KMS) and long-term Private deployment options.

Key metrics to include (data pull notes)
- Monthly tokens: 600M (current) — 3mo trend: +18% QoQ
- 95p response latency (hosted): 420ms overall; during peak windows spikes to 900ms
- Error rate (generation failures): 0.7% overall; correlated with long-sequence (>2048) jobs
- Cost per 1k tokens (hosted): $0.42; projected with Dedicated pilot: $0.28
- Cache hit rate: 62% for prefix caching experiment in last 30 days

High-level narrative (elevator pitch)
- "Horizon has scaled an ambitious clinical summarization pipeline on Redwood. Over Q3-Q4 we helped reduce token spend via caching and started work on a Dedicated pilot to stabilize peak latency. The QBR agenda is to show measurable wins, align on remaining friction (esp. long-seq tails), and propose a committed Dedicated trial to lock in cost predictability while improving 95p latency."

Slide-by-slide outline + speaker notes (draft)
Slide 1: Title / Attendees / Agenda- Speaker note: Quick intros, confirm goals for the call. Keep to 3 bullets.

Slide 2: Topline health snapshot- Visual: 4 KPI tiles (Tokens M/M, 95p latency, Errors %, Cache hit %)- Speaker note: Call out the +18% token growth and acknowledge the spike windows. Reassure: cost engineering moves are working (caching).

Slide 3: Usage & cost trends- Chart: tokens by service / cost by bucket.- Speaker note: Walk through where tokens are concentrated (summarization ~72%, embed+search ~18%). Show current per-1k cost and projected cost with Dedicated pilot.

Slide 4: Latency & reliability deep-dive- Visual: latency percentile graph with peak vs non-peak.- Speaker note: Explain root cause of tail latencies (concurrency + long sequences) and present mitigations: automatic prefix caching expansion, smart routing to Dedicated during peaks.

Slide 5: Customer wins / success highlights- Bullets: 1) 35% faster nightly summarization job since cache tuning; 2) Reduced token leakage in pipeline (saved ~6% cost); 3) Successful integration w/ internal feature store.- Speaker note: Use short customer quotes if available (ask Mateo for a 1-line quote).

Slide 6: Open issues & proposed remediation- Items: KV cache evictions during bursts, occasional 429s for long training jobs, need for HSM integration for certain datasets.- Speaker note: Assign owners (Redwood SRE: Marcus Li; HMR data eng: Mateo Ruiz). Propose timeline: triage (2 weeks), patch (4–6 weeks), monitor.

Slide 7: Renewal health & commercial ask- Visual: renewal health scorecard (Adoption 8/10, Technical Fit 7/10, Exec Alignment 6/10) => Overall "At Risk / Manageable"- Speaker note: Recommend ask: 12-month renewal with optional 6-month Dedicated pilot (15% committed discount; pilot converts to reserved capacity discount if converted).

Slide 8: Expansion opportunities (tie to product)- Bullets: 1) Dedicated reserved pool for peak windows (cost + latency); 2) Redwood Optimize package (batching/quant suggestion); 3) Enhanced observability addon (token-level traces + eval regression alerts).- Speaker note: For each oppty include estimated ARR uplift and a customer benefit statement.

Slide 9: Roadmap alignment & security posture- Bullets: upcoming HSM/KMS GA timeline, Private (VPC) roadmap for 2025 H1, QA for HIPAA-related audit logs.- Speaker note: Reassure legal/procurement. Link to security brief in Confluence.

Slide 10: Next steps & decisions needed- Bullets: 1) Decision on Dedicated 6-month pilot by 2024-11-30; 2) Approval to open procurement conversation for HSM; 3) Confirm pilot success metrics (95p latency target <350ms, cost delta <+5% over baseline).- Speaker note: Capture commitment actions and owners.

Stakeholder-specific talking points (short)
- Dr. Lena Kaur (CTO): Emphasize latency SLOs, architectural fit, private deployment roadmap and HSM timeline. Ask: How critical is sub-350ms 95p to clinical workflows?
- Mateo Ruiz (Head of Data Platform): Focus on operational friction: cache evictions, long-seq jobs, integration with feature store. Offer: a scoped SRE workshop to optimize pipeline (2 weeks).
- Olivia Park (Procurement): Commercial clarity: pilot pricing, conversion terms, SLAs. Provide a clear one-pager (attached) and timeline for PO.

Renewal health assessment (short rationale)
- Signals positive: product adoption, clear cost savings from caching, engaged engineering POC.
- Signals caution: exec alignment not tight (CTO prefers on-prem options), procurement sensitivity to price, technical friction on long sequences impacting key job SLAs.
- Current risk status: Manageable risk — needs executive check-in and concrete pilot signoff.

Proposed commercial motion (recommended)
- 6-month Dedicated pilot: target start 2024-12-15. Pilot terms: capped monthly commit (baseline = existing avg peak usage + 20%), 15% pilot discount.
- Renewal ask: 12-month renewal at discounted committed rate if pilot converts within 60 days post-pilot.
- Add-on: Redwood Optimize consult (3 days) as incentive and scope for measurable SLOs.

Renewal tracker (mini table - text form)
- Opportunity ID: HMR-2025-REN
- Renewal date: 2025-02-14
- Current ARR: $320k
- Target: $380k (with Dedicated conversion + Optimize addon)
- Decision owner: Dr. Lena Kaur
- Procurement owner: Olivia Park
- Next checkpoint: 2024-11-30 (pilot decision)

Open questions / asks for HMR prior to QBR
1) Mateo: can you confirm the 95p latency target for your most critical job? (need numeric)
2) Olivia: expected procurement timeline and PO lead time (target days)?
3) Legal: any additional terms for HSM/KMS that would affect pilot signoff?

Appendix: Suggested pre-send email (to CTO + stakeholders)
Subject: QBR agenda and pilot proposal — Redwood x Horizon Medical Research
Body:
Hi Lena / team,
We’re looking forward to the QBR on [date]. Attached is a short deck and a proposed pilot scope (6-month Dedicated) that we think will address peak latency and give you predictable unit economics. Could you confirm: (1) whether the 95p latency target for your clinical summarization job is <=350ms, and (2) your preferred date for a 30-minute pilot kickoff?
Thanks,
Ava + Customer Success

Notes to internal team (do not send)
- Get updated metric exports from analytics (Ethan) by 2024-11-10.
- Pre-QBR dry run with Marcus + product on 2024-11-20.
- Attach security brief and pilot T&C to SFDC opportunity.

Version history
- v0.1 (2024-11-05) initial draft
- v0.2 (2024-11-09) added metrics and pilot economics (Ethan)
- v0.3 (2024-11-12) updated stakeholder notes and action owners (Ava)

End of doc.
